newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures finish mostly higher.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly higher after a choppy afternoon, with most indices off their earlier session peaks.
September Standard and Poor's 500 futures rallied to 905.00 in early afternoon trade as Treasury bonds strengthened, but stalled there and cut gains the rest of the day.

"This market feels jittery, it's very volatile," an S&P 500 futures trader said. He said S&Ps were prone to wide swings and quick changes of direction as money managers continued to be good buyers and others looked to take profits.

"The last 45 minutes it was really choppy," another trader said. One Chicago-based futures brokerage was a good seller of S&Ps after T-bonds closed, he said. Locals turned active after that, squaring up into the weekend.
Price boards reflected an estimated volume in September S&P 500s of around 70,000 contracts, the trader said.
Most stock index futures started with a firm tone, in line with T-bond strength and a firm dollar. Traders said quarter-end buying and expectations for steady monetary policy next week aided gains.
The Federal Reserve's policy arm meets July 1 and 2. Futures traders said the consensus was for no rise in short-term interest rates.
Also on the agenda next week are national purchasing management and June jobs data and the Independence Day holiday. Trade will close early Thursday at 1215 CDT/1715 GMT and will be shut Friday.

Early in the day, U.S. first-quarter gross domestic product growth was revised to 5.9 percent from 5.8 in the most recent preliminary reading. The University of Michigan's final index of consumer sentiment for June rose to 104.5 from 103.2 in May.

At the close, Sept S&Ps were up 2.65 at 896.90, KCBT Value Lines rose 2.65 to 793.25, NYSE Composites were up 1.35 at 467.85, Nikkeis were flat at 20,625, Midcap 400s were up 2.30 at 290.85, Nasdaq 100s fell 6.00 to 975.15 and Russell 2000s rose 3.10 to 397.00. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))
